requirements.evidence: Most of the contract is implemented: models/factories/enum (app/Models/Entity.php:11-38, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:18-47, app/Models/UserRole.php:5-20), policies (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:11-38, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-38), owner_seq + unique index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_032737_create_entity_memberships_table.php:23-27), routes (routes/web.php:26-39), settings save/delete/transfer (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:37-100) and docs (docs/database-schema.md:91,139,151). Gaps: the add button key ui.add_member does not exist (resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:6) and assignRole can demote the owner, leaving zero owners (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:64).

conventions.evidence: Good: policies registered in AppServiceProvider.php:30-31, $fillable on both models (app/Models/Entity.php:13, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:17), reversible generated migrations, Blade components and Bulma classes, lang keys and docs updated. Deviations: domain writes stay in the components/controller instead of app/Actions (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:45,64; app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:46,52,68), no #[Validate] attributes (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:33-35, app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:41-46), manual authorization in EntityController.php:23-27, and no CHANGELOG.md entry.

security.evidence: Every public action authorizes server-side and validates input: app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:31,58,72, app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:39,54,70, and EntityController.php:25-27; the entity is #[Locked] (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:17-18, app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:18-19) so it cannot be swapped client-side; action IDs are re-scoped to the entity (Members.php:54-55, 68-69); all Blade output uses {{ }}. Residual gap: assignRole does not restrict the target, so the owner row can be demoted (see requirements issue).

tests.evidence: change.diff adds 22 files and none are under tests/; there is no Pest/PHPUnit coverage for the models, policies, pick endpoint, pages or any of the Livewire actions, despite conventions.md requiring a test for every feature plus an unauthorized-call and tamper test for each Livewire action.

simplicity.evidence: Small, direct components that reuse Gate policies and the existing layout/Blade components; minor duplication remains in the check-then-insert duplicate detection (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:39-44) and inline FQCNs (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:94).

readability.evidence: Short focused methods and consistent sibling style; however app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:41 contains a leftover agent note ('Tests likely check error on email'), and app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:74,82 has redundant/confusing role checks.

scope.evidence: All 22 files serve the entities task: models, enum, policies, migrations, factories, Livewire pages and Blade, routes, lang (lang/en/ui.php:47-59, lang/pt_BR/ui.php:47-59) and the required docs/database-schema.md update. No unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, while conventions.md makes tests mandatory for every new behavior and specifically requires unauthorized-call and tamper tests for each Livewire action.

All domain writes (add/assign/remove member, save/delete/transfer) are performed inline in the Livewire components instead of the app/Actions/* use-case classes the conventions mandate, including authorization inside the action.

assignRole validates only the new role, not the target, and the owner row is rendered with the same admin/employee select, so an owner or admin can demote the owner and leave the entity with zero owners, breaking the exactly-one-owner invariant that transfer() is supposed to protect.

The add button uses the key ui.add_member, but only ui.add was added (lang/en/ui.php:57, lang/pt_BR/ui.php:57), so the page renders the raw key or a hardcoded English fallback instead of text from lang/*/ui.php.
The role option labels are hardcoded 'admin'/'employee' rather than coming from lang/*/ui.php, violating the requirement that all screen text come from the lang files.
pick authorizes with a manual membershipFor() check instead of the EntityPolicy/Gate, contrary to the convention that authorization always goes through policies/gates.
The components use inline rule arrays and the global validator() helper instead of the project's #[Validate] + $this->validate() pattern.
A leftover development comment ('Use a clearer duplicate message if available? Tests likely check error on email.') refers to tests that do not exist and should not ship.
The conventions require CHANGELOG.md to be updated under [Unreleased] in the same change, and it is not touched.
The 'owner row vanished' check happens before and outside the DB transaction, so a concurrent ownership change between the check and the updates is not covered by the promised 403.

The manager count includes the target and the owner, so for an admin target it is always at least 2; the last-manager guard is effectively dead except for an owner membership, which the policy already denies.
Duplicate detection is a check-then-insert; a concurrent insert still violates entity_memberships_entity_user_unique and surfaces as a 500 rather than an error on email.

The owner check in removeMember duplicates what EntityMembershipPolicy::delete already denies, and fully-qualified class names (\App\Models\UserRole, \Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB) are inlined instead of imported.

review.summary: The change implements the entities data model, policies, factories, migrations, routes, lang keys, schema docs and the three Livewire pages, and most requirements are covered with server-side authorization and validation. It cannot be approved as is: there is no test at all, domain writes bypass the required app/Actions layer, and assignRole lets the owner be demoted, breaking the exactly-one-owner invariant, alongside smaller lang/UI defects.
